clue.text: Meat pastes — they're for eating

parts.note: chops are cuts of meat such as lamb or pork
to paste something is to stick it, so pastes means sticks

explanation.surface: A remark that meat pastes are there to be eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pastes' reads as a noun in the surface but is a verb here: it pastes, it sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: The pair of thin rods used in East Asian cuisine are utensils for lifting food to the mouth.

clue.text: A top man wants little publicity

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
an ad is a short advertisement, a small piece of publicity

explanation.surface: A senior figure prefers to keep a low profile.
explanation.definitionFit: The uppermost part or the chief of something is called its top or its leader.

clue.text: Left the port — being irritated

explanation.surface: Someone sailed away from the harbour because they were annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that sets off to sea from a harbour has departed; a person annoyed or offended is likewise said to be bothered or upset by it.

clue.text: Changing course and engaging about a hundred

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece goes round the other here

parts.note: engaging in the sense of attractive, winning, is taking
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A sailor alters direction while involving roughly a hundred people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TAKING around C. 'Changing course' is the sailing sense: zigzagging into the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: In sailing, a boat zigzags into the wind by turning its bow through the wind, altering its heading.

clue.text: There's room here — about 45 inches

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
the ell was an old English measure of cloth, 45 inches long

explanation.surface: Someone measures a space and finds it roughly 45 inches across.
explanation.walkthrough: An ELL is an old cloth measure of 45 inches; C (circa) means about.
explanation.definitionFit: A small room, as in a prison or monastery, is a chamber where someone is kept or lives.

clue.text: Tree requiring some maintenance work

explanation.surface: A tree needs a bit of looking after.
explanation.definitionFit: The sorb or wild service is a European tree of the rose family; a routine overhaul of a car or machine is also given this name.

clue.text: Shut up and check on this bloomer!

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means shut up or confined
to stem a flow is to check or stop it
taken as written

explanation.surface: An order to be quiet and look at this flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' sounds like a blunder but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden perennial with tubular flowers, so a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Cite a paper's interpretation of honour

indicators.note: an interpretation gives a new reading of these words, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive ending adds no letters

explanation.surface: Citing a newspaper's reading of an award or tribute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interpretation of' rearranges CITE A PAPER.
explanation.definitionFit: To value or esteem someone highly is to hold them in respect.

clue.text: Shed tears, having little money

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
P stands for penny or pence, British money

explanation.surface: Someone cries because they are nearly broke.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the abbreviation for a penny, the smallest British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry is to let tears fall.

clue.text: Outstanding item

explanation.surface: A notable thing on a list.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of special note is exceptional, and as a noun the word means a detail or single point, as in 'in every respect'.

clue.text: The guy who won?

parts.note: a man's first name that also names whoever came first in a contest

explanation.surface: A question about which man was the winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A winner of a battle or contest is a conqueror, and the word is also a man's given name.

clue.text: Man with guts breaking a horse

indicators.note: breaking smashes these words apart so their letters can be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man with nerve is taming a wild horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges MAN + GUTS; the surface's horse-breaking is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A feral horse of the American plains is a type of horse.

clue.text: Deceived about an employee being improperly treated

indicators.note: about tells us one word goes round the other in this clue

parts.note: misled means deceived
a hand is a worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: An employee was lied to and badly handled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; a hand is an old word for a hired worker, as in deckhand.
explanation.definitionFit: Handled badly or wrongly managed is a synonym for mistreated.

clue.text: A good man, and yet responsible for a stoppage

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a good man
taken as written
still means yet, as in 'still here'

explanation.surface: A virtuous person who nevertheless caused a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete halt, where nothing moves, is a stoppage.

clue.text: Old king taking dope — dope!

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George, on old British postboxes and coins
a dope is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: A former monarch takes drugs: how stupid!
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'dope' means a fool (ASS); the second is slang for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for cannabis or marijuana, a drug.

clue.text: The person most reluctant to give credit

definitions.text: The person most reluctant to give credit

parts.words: The person most reluctant to give credit
parts.note: credit here is belief, not money: this is someone who doubts whatever they are told

explanation.surface: Who is the least willing to lend money?
explanation.walkthrough: 'credit' seems financial, but it means belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubter is someone who withholds belief.

clue.text: The mark of the beast

parts.note: not the Biblical number but a literal trail of footprints or droppings left by a wild animal

explanation.surface: The sign of the Antichrist from Revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase recalls the Book of Revelation, but here it is just an animal's track.
explanation.definitionFit: The trail or track of a wild animal, used by hunters.

clue.text: Grouse mature after the end of spring

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other in the answer
the end of a word is its final letter, taken here from spring

parts.note: ripe means mature

explanation.surface: A game bird grows up after spring ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' looks like the bird but is a complaint; 'after' puts RIPE behind G.
explanation.definitionFit: To grumble or complain, a synonym for grouse.

clue.text: A supporter's suspension

explanation.surface: A comment about someone's backing being put on hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope bracing a mast, or a corset stiffener, is a support; a postponement, as of execution, is a suspension.

clue.text: The girl in love can seem markedly kinder

indicators.note: in tells us the name sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A girl who falls in love may come across as noticeably nicer.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across 'seem markedly'; 'love can' and 'kinder' are surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, as of Jane Austen's heroine.

clue.text: Where sporting people meet when about to retire

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: retire means draw back, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Where sporting folk gather when they are about to call it a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retire' reverses TO to make OT. ASCOT is the racecourse in Berkshire, England, famous for Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous English racecourse, so a venue where racing fans gather.

clue.text: A second subordinate going to pieces

parts.note: under means lower in rank, subordinate

explanation.surface: A deputy in charge is falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart or into fragments, as in torn apart.

clue.text: "X" qualified, so may be retained

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
able means competent, qualified

explanation.surface: Someone named only by an X is qualified, so can be kept on.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable of being held or defended, as a position.

clue.text: Give a talking-to, but dread rocking the boat

indicators.note: rocking shakes up the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a boat

explanation.surface: Speak your mind, though you fear causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocking' rearranges DREAD to ADDRE; 'rocking the boat' looks like one idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak to or lecture someone formally, as in a speech.

clue.text: The French way to receive regular income

indicators.note: to receive means to take in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: rue is French for street
even means regular or steady

explanation.surface: A French custom that brings a steady salary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to receive' is the container signal; 'The French' tempts you towards LE or LA, but the whole phrase 'French way' is the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Money coming in, especially to the state, is income.

clue.text: Former tars negotiated bonuses

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: negotiated means worked out anew, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Ex-sailors bargained for additional pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiated' rearranges TARS to TRAS; tars are sailors in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional items or payments beyond the usual are bonuses.

clue.text: Hold up a letter from Greece and row about it

indicators.note: about it says the second word wraps around the letter just named

parts.note: din means a row, a racket
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Delay a letter from Greece and argue over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about it' is the container signal, 'it' pointing back to the Greek letter; 'row' is the noisy kind, not oars.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep someone back or delay them is to hold them up.

clue.text: Quietly draw the cork?

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
to lug is to drag or draw something heavy

explanation.surface: Gently pull the cork from a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about uncorking; 'cork' is the stopper itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopper for a hole or bottle neck is an example of a cork.

clue.text: Note correction applied in public school

indicators.note: a correction fixes the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A note of reprimand issued at a fee-paying school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correction applied' rearranges NOTE. ETON is England's famous fee-paying boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A prestigious English fee-paying boarding school.

clue.text: Think to entrap?

explanation.surface: Mulling over whether to set a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as DE- (undo) + LIBERATE: to un-free someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder carefully is to weigh things; read as un-freeing, the word jokingly means capture.

clue.text: Fish, or else go crazy

indicators.note: go crazy means the word's letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A threat: produce fish or lose your mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go crazy' rearranges ELSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Long snakelike fish, a kind of fish.

clue.text: Telephone about getting out — and getting back

indicators.note: about tells us one word goes round the other here

parts.note: to ring is to telephone
egress means a way out or the act of leaving

explanation.surface: Phoning about leaving, and then about coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; the two 'getting' phrases look parallel, but the first is wordplay and the second the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Going back to an earlier state is returning.
